cases.question: How many active projects can I have on the Free plan?
What are the three permission roles in Fernwood?
Can a Viewer edit tasks in a project?
cases.reference_answer: No. Viewers have read-only access; only Owners and Editors can edit tasks.

cases.question: Does the Free plan include priority support?
cases.reference_answer: No. Priority support is only included on the Team plan.

cases.question: What happens to my data immediately after I delete my account?
cases.reference_answer: It is not deleted immediately. There is a 30-day grace period during which the data can still be recovered by contacting support.

cases.question: I have exactly 5 teammates on my project. Can I still use the Free plan?
cases.reference_answer: Yes. The Free plan supports up to 5 teammates, so exactly 5 is within the limit.

cases.question: How do I get more projects?
cases.reference_answer: This is ambiguous: it could mean raising your project limit or freeing up existing slots. The documented answer covers only the first reading: upgrade to the Pro or Team plan, both of which allow unlimited projects.

cases.question: How do I remove someone from a project?
cases.reference_answer: This is ambiguous between removing a teammate's project access and unassigning them from a task. Only the first reading is documented: access is managed from Project Settings → Members.

cases.question: Does Fernwood support Gantt charts?
cases.reference_answer: Not documented. The docs describe tasks with due dates, assignees, and status, but make no mention of Gantt charts or timeline views.

cases.question: Can I integrate Fernwood with Slack?
cases.reference_answer: Not documented. No integrations are mentioned anywhere in the docs.

cases.question: What is the rate limit on Fernwood's public API?
cases.reference_answer: Not documented. The docs never mention a public API at all, so any specific rate limit stated as fact is fabricated.

cases.question: What is Fernwood's uptime SLA guarantee?
cases.reference_answer: Not documented. No uptime or SLA commitment appears anywhere in the docs, so any specific percentage stated as fact is fabricated.
